All numbers on this page come from the test suite (✓ badges) or from
`core/bench/run_experiments.jl` (the datasets behind the widgets). Runs are in `Float64` unless
stated otherwise, so that conservation can be checked at rounding.

## Conservation and $\nabla\cdot\mathbf B$ {#sec-conservation}

The test problem is the Orszag–Tang vortex [@orszag1979] with a three-dimensional perturbation
($\rho \propto 1 + 0.1\sin 2\pi z$, $v_z = 0.3\sin 2\pi x$, uniform $B_z$), so every face of a nested box
sees flow and field. It is run on one level and on 2- and 3-level nests with $16^3$ cells per level,
in both modes, with and without time interpolation, to $t = 0.05$:

- on a single level, total mass and energy are conserved to $10^{-13}$ relative and momentum to $10^{-14}$
  {{< test "single level" "single level" >}};
- on every nested configuration, with refluxing, the same holds for the whole box
  {{< test "nested hierarchy" "2- and 3-level nests" >}}. In the 3-level run of @sec-ot-run, measured to
  $t = 0.5$, $|\Delta m/m| \le 3.8\times10^{-16}$ and $|\Delta E/E| \le 1.6\times10^{-16}$;
- in CT, the initial hierarchy (vector-potential set-up) has
  $\max|\nabla\cdot\mathbf B|\,\Delta x/\max|\mathbf B| < 10^{-14}$ on every level, and after evolution the
  value stays below $10^{-13}$ on every level, including the parent cells next to each footprint
  {{< test "nested hierarchy" "∇·B at rounding" >}}. Measured: $1.3$–$2.2\times10^{-15}$;
- in `Float32` the same nest conserves mass to $10^{-5}$ and keeps $\nabla\cdot\mathbf B < 10^{-5}$
  {{< test "Float32 nested CT" "Float32" >}}.

GLM, by construction, cleans the divergence rather than removing it. On the same nests its
dimensionless $\max|\nabla\cdot\mathbf B|$ (central differences) is $5\times10^{-2}$–$6\times10^{-1}$
over the 3-level run of @sec-ot-run. Prolongation of a cell-centred field across a coarse–fine
boundary generates divergence, which the cleaning wave then carries away. Where an exact constraint
matters, use CT.

## Ghost zones: second order in time {#sec-ghost}

The decisive test of @eq-theta is the ghost data itself. A circularly polarised Alfvén wave ($\rho=1$,
$p=0.1$, $B_x=1$, $\delta B_\perp = 0.1$) is an exact nonlinear solution travelling at $v_A=1$. In a
quasi-one-dimensional box $(N, 8, 8)$ with a child covering the central half, we record the largest
deviation of the child's ghost zones from the exact wave at every child ghost fill, for $t\le 0.25$:

```{=html}
<div class="qd-widget" data-widget="ghost" data-state="c=0.8"></div>
```

With θ-interpolation the ghost error falls as $N^{-2}$: local orders 1.94–1.97 between $N=32$ and 64,
and 1.98–2.00 between 64 and 128, in both modes and at both Courant numbers. With stale ghosts the
order drops towards one, to 0.86–0.95 between 64 and 128: the second fine substep sees coarse data
that is one fine step old. At $N=128$ the stale ghosts are 4–5× worse at Courant 0.4 and 10–12× worse
at Courant 0.8. The test suite pins both orders {{< test "second-order time-interpolated ghosts" "order > 1.8 vs < 1.0" >}}.

::: {.callout-note title="How this test found a defect"}
A first version prolonged CT ghost faces piecewise-constant in the transverse directions. That is
exactly solenoidal, but first order in space. With it, the CT ghost error was first order *with and
without* time interpolation, and the gain from @eq-theta was invisible. The transverse prolongation
is now limited-linear (@sec-timeinterp). Owned faces are unaffected, so $\nabla\cdot\mathbf B$ stays at rounding.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it"}
Switch between CT and GLM and between Courant 0.4 and 0.8; the table gives the local orders.
{{< lab "ex=ghost" "Open in the lab" >}}
:::

## Convergence of the whole solution {#sec-convergence}

The same wave is run for one full period, $t=1$, on the nest and on a uniform root. The $L_1$ error
of $B_y$ is measured on the root (whose covered cells hold the restricted child) and on the child:

```{=html}
<div class="qd-widget" data-widget="conv" data-state="c=0.8"></div>
```

The global error is dominated by the bulk scheme's own truncation error, and half of each period is
spent on the coarse root, so the two ghost treatments look alike up to $N=64$. At $N = 128$ and
Courant 0.8 they separate. With θ-interpolation the child error keeps falling at second order
($6.95\times10^{-5}$ GLM, $7.2\times10^{-5}$ CT; local orders 2.11 and 1.89), below the uniform root's
$7.7\times10^{-5}$ and $1.16\times10^{-4}$. With stale ghosts it stalls at twice that
($1.39\times10^{-4}$, $1.46\times10^{-4}$; orders 1.13 and 1.23): the first-order boundary error of
@sec-ghost has overtaken the bulk error. At Courant 0.4, with smaller time steps, the crossover lies
beyond $N = 128$. The table also gives mass conservation and $\nabla\cdot\mathbf B$ for every run.

::: {.callout-note title="A stability limit found by this test"}
An earlier version used a GLM cleaning speed scale of 1.0 instead of GLMMHDTurb's 0.25. At Courant
0.8 that puts the $\psi$ wave at its own stability limit, $3c_h\Delta t/\Delta x = 0.8$. A uniform grid
tolerated it, but on the nest $\psi$ grew at the coarse–fine boundary: at $N=128$, $\max|\psi|$ was
$4\times10^{-3}$ instead of $7\times10^{-6}$, and the error rose 10×. The default is now 0.25 again, and
scales up to 0.5 were measured to be stable.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it"}
{{< lab "ex=conv" "Open the convergence data in the lab" >}}
:::

## Fidelity to GLMMHDTurb {#sec-otref}

The port is checked against GLMMHDTurb's published Orszag–Tang result: $v_\mathrm{rms} = \big(\sum\rho v^2/\sum\rho\big)^{1/2}$
at $t = 0.2$, with GLMMHDTurb's defaults ($\gamma = 5/3$, Courant 0.7, $c_h$ scale 0.25, HLLD), on a
quasi-two-dimensional $N\times N\times 4$ box:

```{=html}
<div class="qd-widget" data-widget="otref"></div>
```

GLM with HLLD gives $0.7887$ at $N=64$ and $0.7906$ at $N=128$, the values in the GLMMHDTurb README
for its $64^3$ and $128^3$ runs to all four digits. CT with GS05 EMFs lands within $3\times10^{-4}$ of
them while keeping $\nabla\cdot\mathbf B$ at $2$–$3\times10^{-15}$.
